item.text: Agence Europe reports that ITRE adopted its position on the European Competitiveness Fund on 10 November by 61 votes to 13 with 12 abstentions, and a negotiating mandate by 56 to 26. It raises the fund to €264bn for 2028–2034.

Agence Europe reports that Friedrich Merz asked António Costa in a letter of 6 November to link fair sharing of the 2027 Ukraine aid gap, about €70bn, to the MFF 2028–2034 talks. Finland and Estonia oppose the link.
Agence Europe reports that ITRE and TRAN adopted their position on the CEF on 10 November by 101 votes to 1 with 17 abstentions. They ask for €91.28bn, against €81.42bn in the Commission proposal.

Agence Europe reports that the committees adopted Marta Temido and Adam Jarubas's report on the directive on GMMs and organs on 10 November by 54 votes to 18 with 16 abstentions. Greens/EFA amendments allowing national bans were rejected.

Agence Europe reports that the Irish Presidency asked ambassadors on 11 November to clarify the partner origin concept, reciprocity and the low-carbon method. No clear majority backs its latest low-carbon compromise.
Agence Europe reports that France, now backed by Germany, wants the Made in Europe scope extended to Switzerland and the United Kingdom. The automotive provisions went to Coreper on 11 November.
MLex reports that IMCO recommended on 10 November, in its opinion on the Digital Omnibus, that cloud providers be exempt from some switching obligations for certain older contracts.

Agence Europe reports that negotiators agreed a five-day deadline for military transport permissions in normal times, but remain split on the crisis framework and EMERS. The next trilogue is set for 9 December.
The Commission presented its proposal for a Digital Fairness Act, an update of EU consumer protection rules so that consumers get the same protection online as offline.
